title: The Asymmetric Harms of LLM Compression
measurement_description: The paper does not specifically measure or evaluate religion. The word 'religion' is mentioned only once as an example of a demographic group when introducing the bias evaluation framework. Although the BBQ benchmark used in the study includes a religion dimension, the paper's reported bias findings focus exclusively on gender, disability, race, and nationality.
findings: There were no specific findings related to religion. The paper's overall findings indicate that model compression causes asymmetric harms: it disproportionately reduces the retention of head knowledge relative to tail knowledge (though head knowledge remains more accurate overall), models remain confidently wrong on knowledge lost during compression, and stable aggregate bias scores conceal large, opposing shifts in stereotypical preferences across non-religious demographic subgroups (such as gender and disability).
